# Shift handover: family-life-chats · 2026-11-12 00:30
> Receiver: run /shift-start first, then read back before acting.
> Previous handover: none · Next-session goal: none given (quick mode, no exam run)

## 0 · Read these first
No files. This was a run of ten unrelated chat sessions, all dated **Fri 2023-03-17**, with no code and no repo work. Repo has only the `start` commit; `.claude/` is untracked [verified: `git status`]. Everything you need is in this file.

## 1 · Status
🟡 Nothing is broken, but several threads stopped mid-way, and some of my earlier answers have errors (§6) that should be fixed if the topic comes up again.

## 2 · Picture
The user asked about everyday-life topics: a niece's birthday party, adopting through foster care in California, gifts, a 401k committee email, breakfast and smoothies, reading on AI in healthcare, Indian evidence and cyber law, Métis support organizations, women in film, and a debate on women in leadership. No single goal ties them together. Answer each new question on its own terms, but use the personal facts in §5. The user expects the assistant to remember them (dates, names, choices).

## 3 · Next actions (open threads, pick up only if the user returns to them)
1. **Hedy Lamarr debate rebuttal**: my answer was cut off mid-sentence ("serve as an important reminder"). Finish it as a short, punchy debate rebuttal. Accurate facts: patent US 2,292,387 (1942), filed with George Antheil, frequency hopping for torpedo guidance. It was a precursor to the spread-spectrum ideas behind Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and GPS, not their direct invention. Done when the user has a usable rebuttal paragraph.
2. **Steve 401k email**: my draft was not in Stephen King style, was not short, and invented a claim ("I do have some experience with FINRA compliance"). The user did not say that. Rewrite it short, in a King-like voice (ominous, plain-spoken, a small-town aside), declining the chair nomination because of no ESRI experience and gently suggesting Steve meant FINRA. Done when the user approves.
3. **Olivia's Art Studio party**: last open question was "what's next" (invitations, games, favors, layout, menu). Pick whichever one the user chooses.
4. **Almond milk**: answered (Almond Breeze, Silk, Califia, Great Value; unsweetened recommended). No open question.

## 4 · No-go zones
| Don't | Why | Reopen only if |
|---|---|---|
| Suggest a princess theme for Olivia | User: "not sure if Olivia would like it… something more unique and not so traditional" | user brings it back |
| Repeat "Merkel has been Chancellor since 2005" | Stale: she left office Dec 2021 | never |
| Say the twins are "already celebrating their first birthday" | Wrong. They were born 2023-02-12, so they were about 5 weeks old on 03-17. Their first birthday is 2024-02-12 | never |

## 5 · Working with the user
**About the user** (all [user said, 2023-03-17] unless noted):
- Niece **Olivia** is turning 6 "soon" and is in kindergarten. The user is planning her party and chose the **Art Studio Party** (the Outer Space Expedition was the runner-up).
- Sister-in-law **Rachel** and the user's brother had twins **Jackson and Julia**, born **2023-02-12**. The user helps with them a lot. The parents were leaning toward **Woodland Wonderland** or **Little Explorer** for the twins' first birthday.
- Cousin **Alex** adopted a baby girl from **China in January 2023**. Alex's agency prioritized birth-mother support and sent updates about the birth mother.
- Lives in **California** and is considering **adopting a baby boy from foster care**. Values agencies that support birth mothers and take a personalized approach.
- Morning routine: wakes **7:30 am**, does **10 minutes of meditation**, then a **30-minute gym workout**. Wants breakfasts under 30 minutes.
- Chose the smoothie, **vanilla** protein, **NOW Foods Whey Protein Isolate** (for price and protein). Plans **Banana-Berry-Mango Bliss** "this weekend" (≈ 2023-03-18/19).
- Getting back into reading after attending a **lecture on AI in healthcare**. Most interested in deep learning for medical imaging. Also curious about AI in research, leadership development and education.
- Working on communication skills. Attended a **communication workshop "at the beginning of last month"** (said 2023-03-17, so early **February 2023**).
- Sits on a **401k committee**. **Steve** offered to nominate the user as next chairperson. The user wants to decline. User's view: Steve probably meant **FINRA** compliance and had **ESRI** (GIS software) on his mind.
- Gifts: graduation gift for a **best friend, $75–100** (custom photo album or personalized jewelry). Small **$10–20** appreciation gifts for coworkers: settled on **funny mugs** and will browse **Zazzle and Redbubble**, possibly phone cases or laptop stickers too.
- Asked law-exam-style questions and said "answer all the questions based on **Indian laws**" [user said]. Probably a student of cyber/evidence law [assumed].
- Asked about support for **Métis** people facing economic hardship and said "I will definitely reach out", so they may be Métis or helping someone who is [assumed].
- Preparing for a **debate** on women's contributions to politics and leadership. Wants rebuttal-style material (Hedy Lamarr). English there was rough, so read their intent generously.

| I did | User signalled | Rule from now on | User's words |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ignored the requested style and length in the Steve email | Asked for short + Stephen King style | Follow explicit style and length constraints literally. Never invent facts about the user | "fairly short and write it in the style of Stephen King" |
| Answered law questions generically | Wanted an Indian law framing | For law questions, cite Indian statutes (Evidence Act 1872 ss.61–65, 65A/65B; IT Act 2000 ss.2(1)(p), 3, 3A, 5, 43, 66) | "answer all the questions based on indian laws" |
| Offered a traditional theme | Wanted something unique | For Olivia, avoid stereotyped "girl" themes | "more unique and not so traditional" |

## 6 · Errors in my earlier answers (correct them if the topic comes back)
- **Indian evidence**: I said hearsay is secondary evidence. Wrong. Under the Indian Evidence Act, s.62 covers primary evidence (the document itself) and s.63 lists secondary evidence (certified copies, mechanical copies, counterparts, oral accounts of contents). Hearsay is a separate issue (s.60, oral evidence must be direct). For electronic records the key rule is the **s.65B certificate** (*Anvar P.V. v. Basheer* 2014; *Arjun Panditrao* 2020). I omitted it.
- **UDRP**: I said "binding, no appeal". The decision is implemented unless a court action is filed within **10 business days** (Policy ¶4(k)). The three elements the complainant must prove were missing: confusingly similar mark, no rights or legitimate interest, registered and used in bad faith (¶4(a)). For .in domains, INDRP applies.
- **AI-healthcare reading list**: *Deep Medicine* (Topol, 2019) is real. "AI Medicine" (Topol & Verghese), "The AI Doctor" (Klasko) and "Healthcare Reboot" (Hoque) are likely **fabricated**. The paper citations are mangled apart from Litjens et al. 2017. Rajkomar et al. 2019 is "Machine Learning in Medicine" (NEJM). The DeepMind mammography claim refers to a Google Health study (McKinney et al., *Nature* 2020). "Haleo" (leadership tool) is likely fabricated.
- **CA adoption**: foster-care adoption in California goes through the county / **Resource Family Approval (RFA)**, which is usually **free**. The $1,500–3,000 home study and 3–6 month figures I gave apply to private agencies. Birth-mother-support framing fits infant or private adoption more than foster care (where reunification is the first goal). Agency names I gave (Adoption Connection, Family Builders, Nightlight) are real agencies, but I did not verify their CA foster-care services [assumed].
- **Métis orgs**: names such as "Métis Nation Financial Wellness Program" and "Métis Capital Housing Corporation" (real, but Alberta-specific) were largely unverified or generic. Point the user to their provincial Métis government (e.g. Métis Nation of Ontario / Métis Nation – Saskatchewan / Otipemisiwak Métis Government in Alberta / MN-BC / Manitoba Métis Federation) [assumed].
- **"ESRI compliance"**: no such 401k term is known. ERISA (Employee Retirement Income Security Act) is the far more likely intended word, more than FINRA. Mention this gently: it is the agent's view. The user's view is FINRA.

## 6b · What I told the user (may be asked again)
- Party themes for Olivia: Art Studio, Backyard Camping, Superhero Academy, Outer Space Expedition, "Outer Worlds Expedition". Art stations: Paint (sponge stamping), Marker (rainbow drawing), Glue (collage), Paper (folding/sculpture). Displays: gallery, clothesline "art walk", collaborative mural, take-home art book.
- Twins themes: Woodland Wonderland, Carnival, Little Explorer, Sweet Treat, Vintage Circus.
- Protein prices quoted: NOW Foods WPI ~$15–20/lb, 20 g protein per scoop. Optimum Nutrition ~$25–30. MusclePharm and BSN ~$20–25.
- Banana-Berry-Mango Bliss = frozen banana + mixed berries + mango + splash of almond milk.
- Mug sites: Zazzle, Redbubble, CafePress, TeeFury, The Oatmeal, Threadless, Society6. Coworker gift ideas: $10–20.
- First US president: George Washington (inaugurated 1789-04-30).
